aliasPolicy: aliases are proposed exact normalization within this atlas; queryExpansions are related search terms, never evidence or automatic label equivalences.
purpose: Research atlas and proposed retrieval rules; not an automatically installed or semantically validated classifier taxonomy.
latestScopeDecision: Flat design and semi-flat variants are included following the user correction.
coverageLimits: Broad documented map, not a universal exhaustive ontology.
Original period, revival, naming, source publication and capture dates are different.
Operational families, community names, official platform systems and surface treatments need different evidence.
No prevalence survey, quality calibration, live collection run or runtime classifier change was performed.

concepts.name: Minimal / minimalist
concepts.definition: Restrained ornament and competing devices, with deliberate hierarchy; information density can still be high.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Swiss / international typographic
concepts.definition: Precise typographic communication organized through systematic alignment and proportional relationships.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Editorial
concepts.definition: Publication-like type, imagery and reading rhythm organize the experience.
concepts.historicalContext: Print lineage; contemporary examples through October 2026.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Refined / luxury
concepts.definition: Composed, material-conscious presentation with controlled emphasis and staged content.
concepts.documentationNote: A retrieval descriptor; price and awards do not establish quality.

concepts.name: Technical / utilitarian
concepts.definition: Instrument-like clarity uses systematic notation and precise information grouping.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Refined tech
concepts.definition: Restrained technological framing combines precision with controlled luminous or dimensional accents.
concepts.documentationNote: Cyberbougie is a related archive nickname; Fluent, glass and neumorphism are distinct.

concepts.name: Neobrutalism
concepts.definition: Orderly graphic boldness combines pronounced outlines, solid offset depth and emphatic type or color.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Raw web brutalism
concepts.definition: Intentional raw digital presentation exposes simple structures or confrontational graphic choices.
concepts.historicalContext: Web vernacular and later deliberate revivals.
concepts.documentationNote: An error-looking screenshot cannot establish intentionality; successful capture and coherent context are required.

concepts.name: Anti-design
concepts.definition: Deliberate graphic dissonance challenges conventional order and presentation.
concepts.documentationNote: Broad critical/retrieval term, not a standardized UI system.

concepts.name: Expressive maximalism
concepts.definition: Visual abundance remains organized by an intentional expressive system.
concepts.historicalContext: Earlier roots; documented designer practices in 2021/2025.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Digital collage / zine
concepts.definition: Assembled cutouts, mixed media and print fragments create a graphic narrative.
concepts.documentationNote: A collage technique can be an imagery tag rather than the whole aesthetic.

concepts.name: Acid graphics / digital rave
concepts.definition: Psychedelic and digital-futurist graphics mix rave motifs, distorted type and synthetic imagery.
concepts.historicalContext: Older psychedelic/rave roots; documented contemporary usage by 2022.
concepts.documentationNote: Digital rave is related vocabulary, not a proven exact synonym.

concepts.name: Retro print / newspaper
concepts.definition: Identifiable period print language is adapted to an interface.
concepts.historicalContext: Historical print references; modern paper-portfolio case.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Geometric pop
concepts.definition: Repeated expressive geometry organizes color and graphic rhythm.
concepts.documentationNote: Do not infer historic Memphis authorship or Material implementation from geometry.

concepts.name: Warm organic
concepts.definition: Natural material, gentle forms and warm textures integrate with controlled content organization.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Romantic botanical
concepts.definition: Botanical ornament and traditional print/type references form a romantic visual world.
concepts.documentationNote: Adobe uses Austere Romanticism for a particular 2021 direction; our family is broader.

concepts.name: Playful tactile 3D
concepts.definition: Soft toy-like forms establish a coherent friendly presentation.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Cinematic
concepts.definition: Staged imagery, atmosphere and composition create a film-like presentation.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Spatial / immersive
concepts.definition: Content appears as a perceptible environment or spatial scene.
concepts.historicalContext: Interactive media roots; current web/native applications.
concepts.documentationNote: A still cannot verify spatial navigation or interaction.

concepts.name: Surreal digital
concepts.definition: Impossible or uncanny relationships among familiar forms create a coherent digital world.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Y2K futurism
concepts.definition: Millennium technological optimism is expressed through synthetic materials and fluid futuristic forms.
concepts.documentationNote: Original references, naming and later revival are separate facts.

concepts.name: Neo-Y2K
concepts.definition: A later revival intensifies or remixes millennium graphic and synthetic forms.
concepts.documentationNote: Pixels alone may establish Y2K-inspired language without establishing original-versus-revival provenance.

concepts.name: Metalheart
concepts.definition: Abstract engineered digital depth recalls the Metalheart/Depthcore-era design milieu.
concepts.documentationNote: Depthcore is also an artist collective/archive; resemblance does not establish membership.

concepts.name: Vectorheart
concepts.definition: Futuristic vector structures and high-contrast utilitarian type convey graphic speed and precision.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Neo-Vectorheart
concepts.definition: A later intensified angular graphic language combines Vectorheart references with gamer/grunge energy.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: McBling
concepts.definition: Early-2000s conspicuous glamour and decorative pop excess organize the visual identity.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Gen X Soft Club
concepts.definition: Muted urbane presentation combines natural tones and understated city/club visual references.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Frutiger Aero
concepts.definition: Glossy humanist technology imagery combines transparent forms with idealized natural worlds.
concepts.documentationNote: Aqua and Windows Aero are related platform languages, not exact aliases for the consumer aesthetic.

concepts.name: Frutiger Eco
concepts.definition: Eco-optimistic glossy technology/nature imagery constructs a harmonious future.
concepts.documentationNote: Qualified community variant; visual imagery does not prove ecological practices or ideology.

concepts.name: Frutiger Metro / vector-pop nostalgia
concepts.definition: Decorative 2000s vector graphics combine flourishes, silhouettes and music/pop motifs.
concepts.documentationNote: Community guides conflate this with Windows Metro; prefer observable traits until a dedicated corpus resolves boundaries.

concepts.name: Vaporwave
concepts.definition: Consumer and early-digital imagery is recombined into surreal nostalgic worlds.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Synthwave / outrun
concepts.definition: Cinematic neon reconstruction of older technological, driving and night-world imagery.
concepts.historicalContext: Internet-era reconstruction of older film/game/music imagery.
concepts.documentationNote: Grouped for retrieval; outrun is a related branch, not an assertion that genres are identical.

concepts.name: Seapunk
concepts.definition: Aquatic fantasy and synthetic nostalgic graphics create an internet-native visual world.
concepts.historicalContext: Creator interview documents the community in 2012.
concepts.documentationNote: Creator context exceeds decorative resemblance; pixels do not establish community membership.

concepts.name: Cyberpunk / neon noir
concepts.definition: Technological urban fiction and human-machine tension shape a speculative visual identity.
concepts.documentationNote: Visible motifs do not prove narrative ideology.

concepts.name: Hexatron / futuristic HUD
concepts.definition: Angular science-fiction instruments combine segmented structures and holographic or terminal-like graphics.
concepts.documentationNote: A fictional HUD picture does not prove interactive application behavior.

concepts.name: Cybercore
concepts.definition: Edited digital nostalgia combines obsolete devices with ethereal or celestial references.
concepts.documentationNote: Do not silently normalize all cyber labels to Y2K; imagery boundaries need examples.

concepts.name: Y3K / speculative hyper-futurism
concepts.definition: Current future-facing graphic/fashion terminology describes speculative synthetic bodies and materials.
counterexamples: A hashtag treated as a mature UI system
concepts.documentationNote: Stable UI boundaries and prevalence are unverified; broad futuristic traits are safer.

concepts.name: Webcore / old-web nostalgia
concepts.definition: Intentional personal-web decoration references early online artifacts and digital self-expression.
concepts.historicalContext: Old-web roots; modern creators documented through 2025.
concepts.documentationNote: Internetcore is a broader query, not an exact synonym; creator labels retain source provenance.

concepts.name: Retro GUI / desktop nostalgia
concepts.definition: Recognizable historical software/window grammar is deliberately reproduced as an interface language.
counterexamples: An embedded screenshot of old software
concepts.historicalContext: Historical GUI references adapted in later design.
concepts.documentationNote: Name a particular OS only with distinctive evidence or provenance.

concepts.name: Pixel / arcade
concepts.definition: Pixel-constructed imagery and period-game graphics organize the presentation.
concepts.historicalContext: Older game roots; continuing internet revivals.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Glitch / corrupted-media language
concepts.definition: Deliberate image/text signal disruption forms a designed visual system.
concepts.historicalContext: Media-art roots; documented artist theory in 2011.
concepts.documentationNote: Datamoshing is a technique; a still cannot establish the codec/process or a transition.

concepts.name: Dreamcore
concepts.definition: Dreamlike associative imagery and hazy familiar environments create ambiguous nostalgic worlds.
concepts.historicalContext: 2020s scenes; older dream-themed art is a precedent, not a proven origin.
concepts.documentationNote: Visual boundary is proposed and culturally variable; dedicated community-aware examples are required.

concepts.name: Weirdcore
concepts.definition: Disorienting familiar imagery and ambiguous digital/text relationships create intentional unease.
concepts.documentationNote: The aesthetic and an artist named Weirdcore are different facts; do not infer mental state.

concepts.name: Liminal-space atmosphere
concepts.definition: Empty familiar or transitional spaces create a suspended uncanny atmosphere.
concepts.historicalContext: Older conceptual roots; contemporary nostalgic scenes.
concepts.documentationNote: Primarily imagery/mood context, not a complete UI system.

concepts.name: Solarpunk / eco-futurism
concepts.definition: Craft and technology coexist within an inhabited ecological-future world.
concepts.historicalContext: Formative artist vision documented in the 2010s.
concepts.documentationNote: Eco-futurist is broader vocabulary; imagery cannot certify sustainability or ideology.

concepts.name: Cottagecore
concepts.definition: Idealized pastoral craft and domestic/natural imagery form a romantic escape.
concepts.historicalContext: Pandemic-era creative-direction context; exact first use not asserted.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Dark academia
concepts.definition: Literary/collegiate references form a moody antique scholarly world.
concepts.historicalContext: Modern internet usage; exact first-use dates unsettled.
concepts.documentationNote: Do not infer education, audience or cultural identity from this styling.

concepts.name: Light academia
concepts.definition: A proposed query variant for airy bright treatments of a literary/collegiate visual world.
concepts.documentationNote: Query expansion only; no independently reviewed UI boundary is established here.

concepts.name: Kawaii / character-led cute
concepts.definition: Coherent charming character/forms emphasize softness and expressive approachable proportions.
concepts.historicalContext: Older Japanese roots; continuing digital adaptations.
concepts.documentationNote: Visual resemblance does not establish Japanese authorship or a specific subculture.

concepts.name: Kidcore
concepts.definition: Childhood/toy nostalgia combines exuberant graphics with a coherent play world.
concepts.documentationNote: Community-source definition; broader UI sampling is required.

concepts.name: Scene / MySpace-era grunge
concepts.definition: A possible cluster combines personalized 2000s profile graphics with distressed pop excess.
concepts.documentationNote: Research lead, not an established classifier class; cybergrunge overlaps without being identical.

concepts.name: Cybersigilism
concepts.definition: Sharp organic/digital ornament produces a sigil-like graphic vocabulary.
concepts.documentationNote: Tattoo/streetwear evidence is not evidence of a complete UI language or UI prevalence.

concepts.name: Flat
concepts.definition: Planar interface graphics use little simulated physical depth.
concepts.historicalContext: Early-2010s adoption with older graphic roots.
concepts.documentationNote: Can span many aesthetics, densities and quality levels.

concepts.name: Semi-flat / selective depth
concepts.definition: Mostly planar graphics use limited dimensional cues for groups or actions.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Skeuomorphic
concepts.definition: Physical-object conventions are adapted to interface controls or roles.
concepts.historicalContext: Older GUI roots; 2000s prominence and later selective use.
concepts.documentationNote: Realism and role-supporting physical metaphors are distinguishable; resemblance alone may not establish behavior.

concepts.name: Apple Aqua
concepts.definition: Apple's named desktop language introduced luminous and semi-transparent controls.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Glassmorphism
concepts.definition: Translucent foreground panels form visible frosted/background-dependent layers.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Neumorphism
concepts.definition: Paired shading makes controls appear inset into or extruded from continuous material.
concepts.historicalContext: Late-2010s UI discussion; later selective applications.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Claymorphism
concepts.definition: Inflated rounded forms combine internal shading with external separation.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Fluent material system
concepts.definition: Microsoft's named system assigns different roles to solid, acrylic, mica and dimming materials.
concepts.documentationNote: Mica is opaque/tinted; acrylic is translucent. A still cannot verify implementation or focus behavior.

concepts.name: Apple Liquid Glass
concepts.definition: Apple's named adaptive optical/translucent material supports a content-oriented software system.
counterexamples: A still claimed to prove adaptation
concepts.documentationNote: Inspired appearance and native material are different claims; stills cannot establish motion, lensing or implementation.

concepts.name: Material Design
concepts.definition: Google's named system combines paper-like surfaces with consistent spatial and behavioral hierarchy.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Material 3 Expressive
concepts.definition: Google's expressive component system emphasizes shape, color and task hierarchy.
concepts.documentationNote: Generic expressive traits can be labeled independently; platform identity requires provenance.

concepts.name: Austurbane
concepts.definition: A curator category combines restrained urbane refinement with staged tactile/natural materials.
counterexamples: Gen X Soft Club treated as identical
concepts.documentationNote: Keep archive vocabulary searchable while prioritizing clear visible traits.

concepts.name: Blob World
concepts.definition: A curator category describes unusual soft rendered worlds that can feel playful or uncanny.
concepts.documentationNote: Operational visual rule synthesized for retrieval; not a validated classification boundary.

concepts.name: Polychrome / fluid-color imagery
concepts.definition: Fluid pigment, smoke or liquid-like color mixing shapes imagery or surfaces.
concepts.documentationNote: Primarily imagery/appearance; not sufficient for a whole-page aesthetic.

concepts.name: Corporate expressive illustration
concepts.definition: A consistent illustrative character/shape language supports brand communication.
concepts.documentationNote: Alegria is a specific creator/system context, not an alias for all illustration.

concepts.name: Clean
concepts.definition: Controlled grouping and hierarchy reduce interference while keeping content readable.
concepts.documentationNote: Independent of aesthetic and date; a rich retro interface can be clean.
